subject: economics
title: Income & Outgoings Adventure
welcome_lead: Money in, money out — meet your budget. 💷
meta_desc: Personal Budgeting Adventure 1 — KS3 Economics on income, outgoings and a simple budget.
final_note: You learned what income and outgoings are and how to build a basic budget.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Income is money coming in.

At your age it might be:

  • Pocket money/allowance.
  • Birthday gifts.
  • Cash for chores or a paper round.

Outgoings are money going out:

  • Sweets and drinks.
  • Games and apps.
  • Travel and clothes.
  • Birthday gifts you buy.

A simple budget compares income and outgoings.

Income £20, outgoings £15 → £5 surplus. 🎉

Income £20, outgoings £25 → £5 deficit. Time to cut back or earn more.

mcqs.q: How does the sign of cross elasticity of demand (XED) reveal product relationships?
options: XED measures how often consumers cross-shop between stores.
Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.
The sign of XED doesn't matter — only the size does.
Positive XED = substitutes (price of one rises, demand for the other rises); negative XED = complements (price of one rises, demand for the other falls); zero XED = unrelated goods.

sequence.def: Add up all money coming in
Positive means saving; negative means overspending
